observations: 52d trajectory improves all36 autonomous1s voltage cases versus52cDE, pooled0.9027315661 to0.7304144619mV, but all36 remain strict failures.
Ih current magnitude is about3.3percent of reference at the initial sample and1.3percent over500-1000ms; imposed V/Ca does not remove suppression.
Missing events persist under imposed inputs; this is not solely autonomous feedback or a small peak-time offset.
Calcium pooled error worsens0.425percent; SK_E2 and some other channel errors worsen despite voltage improvement.
All trajectory/combined seeds selected300 rather than800updates. This does not establish convergence or prove that longer training cannot help.

hypotheses.claim: Frozen encoding and decoder calibration fail to preserve current amplitude before recurrence; a dynamics-only repair is insufficient.
hypotheses.test: Before training, compare initial readout, exact-state re-encoding, and best free-latent readout on fit/development states only. For scalar Ih scan its full bounded latent coordinate. Free latent is diagnostic, never deployed or used for fresh selection.
hypotheses.discriminator: Good free-latent readout but poor exact-state encoding indicates encoder alignment; poor free-latent fit suggests decoder limitation; accurate t0 but later drift suggests dynamics. A failed numerical search is not a proof of impossibility.

hypotheses.claim: Short randomly sampled windows and opening-weighted samples underrepresent long Ih relaxation and brief high-current transients.
hypotheses.test: Factor S: replace a fixed fraction of ordinary examples with canonical fit-only long hyperpolarization/rebound/recovery and transient windows, with paired total examples, updates and compute. Maintain ordinary replay.
hypotheses.discriminator: S improves unseen protocols and the relevant current/event strata, beyond additional generic training, without relying on fresh-case-specific mining.

hypotheses.claim: Family averaging and joint updates permit weak channels or current events to be sacrificed while autonomous voltage improves.
hypotheses.test: Factor G: add family-resolved current/charge/peak objectives, retaining the autonomous objective and original per-channel metrics. Normalize using fit-only scales, not changed acceptance thresholds. Apply the same development non-regression selection rule to all four arms, so selection is not confounded with G.
hypotheses.discriminator: G improves worst-channel errors and suppresses regression; record gradient norms/cosines to separate insufficient gradient from conflicting gradient. If no checkpoint qualifies, retain baseline and report no improvement.

hypotheses.claim: 12.8ms truncated gradients are too short for slow memory even when the forward trajectory is longer.
hypotheses.test: Shared fit/development diagnostic compares short and longer truncated-gradient horizons at fixed state; log gradient signal for Ih. Use nested budget checkpoints. Promote a longer horizon to a separate registered factor only if this probe supports it; do not conflate it with support factor S.
hypotheses.discriminator: A changed long-horizon gradient direction/signal and reduced slow-tail error supports credit assignment; merely running a longer forward pass does not test it.

hypotheses.claim: Part of the voltage fit relies on compensating errors across currents, so correcting a single family may reveal rather than create another error.
hypotheses.test: Shared nonselectable frozen-current substitutions for Ih, Ca, their combination and all currents; compare per-channel residual signs, net residual and autonomous response before and after repair.
hypotheses.discriminator: A substitution that improves a channel but worsens voltage, with opposite-sign residuals in another family, supports compensation. Substitution effects are local to the tested model and do not prove a unique mechanism.

proposed_matrix: G: family-resolved loss and non-regression selection
shared_controls: Same52d trajectory initialization, seeds, architecture, frozen encoder initially, decoder+recurrence trainable, common minibatch schedule where possible. Same total budget; nested checkpoints. Common development non-regression selection against the baseline for all four arms. Preserve an unchanged frozen52d trajectory reference. Diagnostics may identify an encoder issue but do not silently unfreeze it.
evaluation: Separate fit/development from fresh protocols. Keep all original current/timing/physical/voltage/calcium gates. Report initial, imposed, autonomous, event peak/charge, long-tail, every family, every case, paired regressions, and atomic cost. Casewise voltage/calcium guard is additional to, not replacement for, strict gates. Zero-current and oracle substitutions remain nonselectable controls.
limitations: 52d reused the52 coupled evaluation panel; its improvements are exploratory. Proposed factors are hypotheses, not established causes. Initial suppression does not identify decoder versus encoder on its own. No guarantee of improvement or no regressions; unsuccessful arms remain failures. Notebook implementation and launch require next user instruction.
